newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Dec 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The appointment of secretary of the Federal Department of Employment, Education, Training and Youth Affairs, Sandy Hollway, to the Sydney Olympics organising committee yesterday triggered a political row, with New South Wales Opposition spokesman on the Olympics Ian Armstrong saying the committee was in danger of becoming a "who's who of the Labor Party". Page 3.

Australian Football League communications manager Tony Peek confirmed yesterday the code has already commenced moves to use the A$665 million Sydney Olympic Stadium for a second Sydney team after the 2000 Games in opposition to the Sydney Swans. Page 21.

Some of Australia's most prominent cricketers believe poor programming may be damaging their careers and their views will be presented to the Australian Cricket Board at a meeting during the Melbourne Test late this month, via the newly reformed Australia Cricket Players' Association. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

According to Australian Cricket Board chief executive Graham Halbish, a proposal brokered in London in recent weeks by New Zealand Cricket Association chief Sir John Anderson to revamp the International Cricket Council and resolve its chairmanship deadlock is no certainty to gain ICC ratification. Page 39.

Susie O'Neill, who contested six events at the Atlanta Olympics and came home with a full set of Olympic medals, gold, silver and bronze, was named Australian Swimmer of the Year yesterday and received her award with trademark humility, saying she was very proud. Page 39.

The West Indies recovered some of their dignity yesterday as they won their first victory in an international this season with a seven-wicket win over Pakistan at Adelaide Oval. Pakistan were all out for 176. Page 40.
THE AGE

Australian touring car driver Neil Crompton, who has raced a Holden Commodore for Wayne Gardner Racing in the Australian touring car championship for the past three years, has joined the exodus of local talent, including Bathurst winner Craig Lowndes and Formula Ford champion Mark Webber, seeking racing success overseas next year. Page C6.

Daniel Kowalski, who won three Olympic medals in Atlanta, has given up his Victorian Institute of Sport scholarship, which is funded by the Commonwealth Bank and where he was named Victorian athlete of the year, in favour of a lucrative private sponsorship with the National Australia Bank. Page C6.

Only weeks after federal government funding was slashed from athletics, the Coalition and the Australian Sports Commission have announced they will be granting the Australian Football League more than A$1 million to establish a football academy and a hall of fame. Page C8.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Football League communications manager Tony Peek has revealed Ross Oakley, the league's departing chief executive officer, has been appointed by the commission as its consultant on the A$250 million Victoria Stadium. Page 96.

More than a dozen people in the racing industry, including Victoria's leading trainer Lee Freedman, have been interviewed by police in relation to an inquiry on racehorse swabbing procedures - sparked by high bicarbonate levels in a Freedman-trained horse at Moonee Valley in September. Page 94.

American point guard Billy McCaffrey, one of the heroes of the Magic's second season National Basketball League title last month, has quit the club to try and make his mark in the National Basketball Association. Page 94.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Racing Industry Wagering Reform Group, representing all three horse racing codes and chaired by Bob Charley, yesterday made public its presentation to the state government of the potential benefits of New South Wales Wagering Reform and TAB privatisaton - including the implementation of a state breeders' incentive scheme. Page 86.

German swimmer Sandra Voelker, 22, who has been called the best swimmer in Europe and who won the European short-course championships last weekend, is due to train in Perth next month in preparation for the world short course championships in Gottenburg next April. Page 85.

Weary after a tough year on and off the golf course, Brett Ogle has announced he plans to return to the Australasian tour full time after he ends a self-imposed exile from the sport at the Heineken Classic inn Perth in late January. Page 80.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
